revision.author: 0x8432319097D7365a686167Bab33d7425B356b2b2
revision.title: EEZ Extends Ethereum: Making Its Contracts Safe for Chains to Adopt
revision.summary: EEZ extends Ethereum, and Ethereum's security with it. EEZ turns cross-chain execution into an Ethereum primitive: rollups and L1 call each other in one transaction, checked on Ethereum with no bridge in between, and a protocol deploys once instead of on every chain. This grant takes EEZ from audit to adoption: an independent audit and fixes, a testnet where outside chains can try the audited contracts, and a final payment only when an external chain or protocol decides to run EEZ on mainnet. Our mission is to deliver an open-source model, within a non-profit framework, that is secure enough for everyone to use; its adoption rests on shared risk, which requires shared security, shared funding, and shared collaboration.

sections.why:
Some of the largest losses in Ethereum's history happened at its bridges: honeypots of locked funds guarded by small signer sets that rely on reputation rather than contract logic or validity proofs, prioritizing UX over security. Ronin, Poly Network, BNB Bridge, Wormhole, and Nomad all sit near the top of the [Rekt leaderboard](https://rekt.news/leaderboard/), and each broke the layer that decides which cross-chain messages are valid. 

EEZ turns cross-chain execution into an Ethereum primitive. A contract on one rollup calls a contract on another rollup, or on L1, and uses the return value in the same transaction, with the result checked on Ethereum. That takes the bridge out of these flows:

* **Moving assets between rollups**, with no third-party contract holding pooled funds under a signer set.
* **Atomic multi-chain actions**, such as a swap funded from another rollup, which complete fully or revert.
* **One deployment serving every chain.** The Balancer v2 exploit drained the same duplicated code chain by chain. With EEZ a protocol deploys once, and a fix applies everywhere.

The clearest win is a smaller attack surface. Today a protocol deploys a copy of itself on every network it wants to reach, and duplication breeds bugs: version drift, per-chain initialization mistakes, maintenance across every copy. The Balancer v2 exploit drained the same duplicated code chain by chain. With EEZ a protocol can deploy once, on the network where it is easiest to control, audit, and secure, and every chain uses it through atomic cross-chain communication. 

Every Layer 2 becomes a true extension of Ethereum: one account and one contract address everywhere, with each network keeping the security guarantees it chooses and better UX than reputation-based bridges. Ethereum L1 stays as secure as it is today, since its consensus does not depend on EEZ. Every connected chain relies on one small contract set on Ethereum, which is easier to audit and monitor than many bridges; that shared risk calls for shared, independent review before chains adopt it, and this grant funds it.

How EEZ changes where security comes from:

* **Each chain picks its verification.** A rollup declares the proof systems it accepts and how many must agree, and every cross-chain action settles against that check on Ethereum. Rollups that run based, like the first Gnosis deployment, go further: sequencing happens inside the L1 block, and anyone can rebuild the chain from L1 data alone.
* **Results are checked on L1.** Every cross-chain outcome is computed ahead of time and checked on Ethereum, so a forged result fails and an operator can at most stall calls. Today one attestation signer runs the check by re-executing each block window; with several proof systems and a threshold, one prover's bug does not compromise the chain. The audit covers both.
* **Wallets** can route cross-chain sends automatically, so funds sent to the right address on the wrong chain stop being a loss.
* **No half-done state.** A cross-chain call and its return value execute in one transaction. Everything commits or nothing does, so stuck funds and partial-state exploits are removed by design.

EEZ is not a dapp and not a product. It is an Ethereum public good: an open, permissionless protocol and infrastructure for synchronous composability between Ethereum rollups. The core EEZ contract has no admin role. Each connected rollup keeps its own contract, whose owner sets the accepted proof systems, verification keys, and threshold; reviewing those privileged roles and how they can be locked down is part of this audit. That design puts the security of the whole system on its smart contracts, which is exactly what this initiative puts under independent review.
sections.in_scope:
* **Independent audit** of the EEZ core contracts at one pinned commit, including privileged roles, cross-chain behavior, and the single attestation signer live today with the multi-prover design it plugs into. Fixes by the EEZ team, re-review by the auditor. About 8 to 10 senior-auditor-weeks; report within 2 months of the auditor's appointment.
* **Integration environment:** the audited contracts on a public testnet, integration docs, a conformance suite, a reference integration, and a support channel. Celo, Polygon, and Linea build their own integrations; this grant pays none of that.
* **Integration support** for the first outside chain or protocol that goes to mainnet.
sections.out_scope:
* Rollup node software, provers, sequencers, and other off-chain infrastructure
* The internal economics of connected rollups
* Re-auditing changes made after the pinned commit
sections.team:
The EEZ Association does the work and is accountable for the outcome.

* [Jordi Baylina](https://x.com/jbaylina), core contributor
* [Friederike Ernst](https://x.com/tw_tter), co-initiator
* [Eduardo Antuña](https://x.com/eduadiez), core contributor
* [Jesús Ligero](https://x.com/JesusLigero3), core contributor
* [Armagan Ercan](https://x.com/epochzer0), coordinator

Other funding: Gnosis commits $30,000 to this goal and hosts the testnet nodes; the $10,000 milestone covers the contract deployment, documentation, conformance suite, and reference integration built on top.
sections.why_grant:
* The protocol is built and public at [eez-core-protocol](https://github.com/eez-association/eez-core-protocol): contracts, specifications under `docs/`, end-to-end test scenarios, and open findings from internal review. The contracts are prepared for devnets and ready for audit.
* GnosisDAO [approved GIP-153](https://snapshot.org/#/s:gnosis.eth/proposal/0x5522f4cbd034c966a08d6901b05c7ad7300041b3e0d75a0ad3da868af1a98b98), making Gnosis Chain the first governance-backed adopter.
* [Celo](https://celo.org/), [Polygon](https://polygon.technology/), and [Linea](https://linea.build/) have agreed in discussions with us to test the audited contracts.
* Vitalik Buterin stress-tested the design with Jordi Baylina at ETHPrague 2026 ([fireside](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=prgWmgUbSVQ)) and called EEZ "a quite helpful effort" at Dappcon Berlin ([panel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gfG-R8AOu0E)). Joseph Lubin supports EEZ publicly ([post](https://x.com/etheconomiczone/status/2052390993610133513)).
sections.commitments:
* **License:** MIT, with a LICENSE file at the repository root.
* **Maintenance:** the EEZ Association maintains the contracts and the public security record after the grant; the testnet stays public for at least 12 months after the report.
* **Pinned target:** at least 1 outside chain or protocol from the adoption list runs EEZ on mainnet within 12 months of the audit report.
* **Independent auditor:** we publish a shortlist of at least 2 firms and why we chose one; the auditor has no ties to the EEZ Association, its contributors, Gnosis, or ZisK.

milestones.name: Independent audit
criteria: Auditor's written independence statement published before work starts
Audit report published for the pinned commit
Every critical and high finding fixed, with the auditor's re-review published

milestones.name: Integration environment
criteria: Audited contracts live on a public testnet, with docs and a conformance suite passing in public CI
Reference integration published: a test chain connected using only the docs, with transactions on a public explorer

milestones.name: Production adoption
criteria: At least 2 outside chains run the audited contracts on mainnet, from this list: Celo, Polygon, Linea, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Robinhood Chain, shown by deployment addresses and each chain's public announcement
At least 4 dapps use EEZ on mainnet, from this list: Aave, Uniswap, Lido, Safe, CoW, Morpho, Sky shown by their deployed integrations and each team's public announcement.
Transactions from users outside that team replace a named bridge-dependent flow, confirmed by the independent reviewer on a public explorer
